name: Clap / Plyometric Push-Up
description: The clap push-up is a plyometric variation in which the pressing phase is explosive enough to launch the hands off the floor, allowing a clap before landing. This develops upper-body power, rate-of-force development, and reactive strength in the chest, triceps, and anterior deltoids through a true stretch-shortening cycle.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard push-up position with hands shoulder-width apart and body in a straight line.
execution.setup_instructions: Perform on a firm, flat surface that provides enough friction for a safe hand landing. Ensure there is adequate floor space.
steps: Step 1: Lower into the bottom of a push-up under control.
Step 2: At the bottom, explosively press the floor away with maximum force.
Step 3: Drive the torso upward fast enough for the hands to leave the floor.
Step 4: Clap the hands together while airborne.
Step 5: Land with hands in the original position, absorbing impact by bending the elbows immediately into the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the way down. Exhale explosively on the press.
common_mistakes: Not lowering enough before the explosive press, reducing power output
Attempting this exercise without sufficient standard push-up strength
safety_considerations: Master push-ups with a minimum of 20 consecutive reps before attempting plyometric variation
Land with bent elbows to absorb impact
Perform on a padded or non-slip surface
Do not perform to failure — stop well before form breaks
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth on the descent. The press must be explosive enough to generate meaningful air time.
coaching_cues: Push the floor through the Earth
Land soft — absorb with the elbows
Quality over quantity — explosive intent every rep
